text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Kenyans face an uncertain day with a national strike called by the opposition-backed alliance the National Convention Executive Council (NCEC) on Friday to press for constitutional reforms before general elections scheduled for later this year.
- The government says a five-day go-slow by air-traffic controllers has been called off.

- A group of senators from the United States of America write to President Daniel arap Moi commending him for opening up dialogue with opposition leaders, but urging him to hasten the constitution reform process.
- The government declares Friday's national strike called by the NCEC illegal.
- Kenya's ambassador to the United States is recalled.

- Finance minister Musalia Mudavadi announces crisis measures aimed at stabilising a turbulent foreign exchange market following the Kenyan shilling's plunge to an all-time official low against the dollar and pound.
- Officials of the ruling party and labour minister urge Kenyans to shun an illegal strike called for Friday by the NCEC.
- A 16-man delegation of members of parliament from the ruling party Kenya African National Union hold a historic meeting with 15 religious leaders.
- A Saudi Arabian princess is charged with allegedly defrauding a Nairobi businessman of at least 33 million shillings.
- Details emerging from insiders paint a picture of a power struggle in State House, cabinet and the battle for supremacy in the Rift Valley.
- Confusion over the national strike continues as pro-reform agitators differ over its timing.
